title: Synthetic Identity Audit: document:9702606:synth_child_e

investigation_findings.why_it_exists: In scenario_e_multi_resource (scripts/f0_25a2_physical_scenarios.py), the author wanted to verify nested child tracking (document under parent window) during a multi-instance launch. Instead of inspecting real UIA document elements from Character Map or Notepad, the author manually synthesized and injected a fake ResourceIdentity with uia_id="synth_child_e".
investigation_findings.why_it_violates_invariants: The scenario was executed and published as a live physical test in F0_25A2_MULTI_RESOURCE_RESULTS.json. Presenting mock or manually synthesized objects within physical evidence contaminates the execution-truth oracle and falsifies empirical verification.
investigation_findings.remedy: Synthetic data is strictly quarantined to UNIT_SYNTHETIC tests. Physical scenarios must observe ONLY authentic Win32/UIA entities returned from operating system APIs (EnumWindows, UI Automation tree inspection, psutil).

UNIT_SYNTHETIC.description: Pure isolated unit tests using synthetic/mock identities, in-memory databases, and stubbed capabilities.

SOURCE_INTEGRATION.description: Integration tests checking interface contracts, schemas, registry lookups, and serialization across modules without live desktop interaction.

PHYSICAL.description: Physical execution against live Windows desktop apps (Notepad, Character Map, etc.) observing authentic HWNDs, PIDs, Win32 window text, and UIA trees.

MODEL_CAUSAL.description: Closed-loop execution guided by local/remote SLM/LLM inference where model outputs govern actions and update Hermes experiential memory.

FROZEN.description: Post-freeze verification against the packaged PyInstaller binary/installer running in an isolated environment.
